title: A module spanned by simple submodules has complements
statement: Let $R$ be a unital ring, not necessarily commutative, and let $M$ be a left $R$-module. An $R$-submodule is an additive subgroup closed under multiplication by every element of $R$ [def-weil-submodule-span]. Call an $R$-module simple if it is nonzero and its only submodules are zero and itself. Suppose $M$ is the sum of all its simple $R$-submodules: every element of $M$ is a finite sum of elements each belonging to a simple submodule. Then every $R$-submodule $N\subseteq M$ has an $R$-submodule complement $P\subseteq M$, so $M=N\oplus P$ (that is, $N+P=M$ and $N\cap P=0$). This includes $M=0$.
